claims: FR-01 in SAP Commerce Cloud: the guided finder is an extension of the product search with four question steps, size M.
FR-02 in SAP Commerce Cloud: the registration form takes the consent in the standard; the shop only passes it on, size S.
FR-03 in SAP Commerce Cloud: the order history shows the delivery status in the standard account pages, size S.
TA-02 is a gap in SAP Commerce Cloud: the shop receives raw ERP status codes and keeps no mapping table for them.
TA-03 is a gap in SAP Commerce Cloud: no service of the shop can feed recommendations into CMS pages.
IF-03 is a gap in SAP Commerce Cloud: real-time points need an interface the loyalty engine does not offer.

client.issue: The finder's four questions include the terrain type, which the product data does not carry yet (requirement list, FR-01 acceptance 2).
client.accept_if: The claim names the missing attribute and whether its maintenance is part of the size.

claims: FR-01 in Shopware: the guided finder is built as a custom plugin on the product listing, size L.
FR-02 in Shopware: the registration form takes the consent with the standard newsletter setting, size S.
FR-03 in Shopware: the order overview shows the delivery status in the standard account, size S.
TA-02 in Shopware: the order states are configurable, so the ERP codes map in the shop's state machine, size M.
IF-03 in Shopware: the account shows imported bonus points with a small plugin, size S.
FR-02 in SAP Customer Data Cloud: consents are stored and versioned per purpose in the standard consent vault, size S.
TA-01 is a gap in SAP Customer Data Cloud: the registration screens offer no confirmation step for consents.
The consent screens are configured, not programmed; the shop embeds them through the standard web SDK.
FR-03 in the Integration Suite: one flow per parent option carries the order status from the ERP to the shop, size M.
TA-02 routed by the architect: the flow translates the ERP status codes with a value mapping, size S.
IF-03 in the Integration Suite: the nightly points file is moved to the shop with the standard file adapter, size S.
IF-03 reduced to the standard: the account shows the points of the nightly import with the date of the last update, size S.
The reduced variant needs no new interface; it reads the points the integration flow delivers.
TA-01 overruled: the consent confirmation runs with the standard double opt-in e-mail templates, size S.
The confirmation e-mail is a template in the deliverable language; no custom code is needed.
Scenario SAP Commerce Cloud costs less in development than scenario Shopware; the difference is driven by the guided finder and the order states.
The surcharges are computed per system option; the fixed phases name their system.
Open inputs: the CMS agency fills three cells, the UX team four, the client one (the SAP BTP service).
The estimate rests on three client assumptions (A-01 to A-03); none of them moves the order of the scenarios.

narrative.md:
## Where we are
The scope step is applied: every requirement has its systems and an impact text per system. Wave 1 estimates SAP Commerce Cloud, Shopware and SAP Customer Data Cloud; the Integration Suite follows once both shop options are final.

## Confirmed so far
- 8 rows, 14 impacts; the printed catalogue touches no system of this run.
- Consents live in SAP Customer Data Cloud; the shop only passes them on.

## Risks of the run
- SAP Customer Data Cloud reported a gap: no confirmation step for consents. The architect decides after wave 1.

## Decisions that would help most
- Is the e-mail confirmation of consents needed in every country? (recommended: yes)

entries.text: Effort is a T-shirt size per work package; person days come from the size mapping of the workbook.
Consents and customer identities are owned by SAP Customer Data Cloud; the shop never stores them.

gate_checks.label: Process language
gate_checks.doc: No wording from the run's own process (rounds, claims, critics) appears in the customer edition.

gate_checks.label: Code vocabulary
gate_checks.doc: Class names, file paths and other code vocabulary are explained or left out.

gate_checks.label: Internal locators
gate_checks.doc: Locators point to what the client can open, not to the run's internal files.

gate_checks.label: Run shorthand
gate_checks.doc: No abbreviations that only the run team uses.

gate_checks.label: Dangling ids
gate_checks.doc: Every id that is mentioned exists on a sheet of the workbooks.

gate_checks.label: Missing sheet references
gate_checks.doc: Every sheet that a cell refers to exists in the workbook.

gate_checks.label: Raw keys
gate_checks.doc: Technical keys are shown as labels a reader understands.

gate_checks.label: Empty columns
gate_checks.doc: No column is empty in every row.

gate_checks.label: Summary numbers
gate_checks.doc: Every number in a summary matches the figures it summarises.

gate_checks.label: Missing summaries
gate_checks.doc: Every sheet that needs a summary has one.

gate_checks.label: Hard-coded totals
gate_checks.doc: Totals are formulas, not typed numbers.

gate_checks.label: Formula errors
gate_checks.doc: No cell shows a formula error.

gate_checks.label: Reconciliation
gate_checks.doc: Figures that appear on two sheets are the same on both.

gate_checks.label: Basis present
gate_checks.doc: Every row states the basis it rests on.

gate_checks.label: Basis from the code
gate_checks.doc: A basis that cites the code names a locator the reader can open.

gate_checks.label: Basis from a source
gate_checks.doc: A basis that cites a source names the document and the place in it.

gate_checks.label: Basis from an assumption
gate_checks.doc: A basis that rests on an assumption names the assumption.

gate_checks.label: Emphasis budget
gate_checks.doc: Bold and colour are used sparingly, so that what matters stands out.

gate_checks.label: Header tiers
gate_checks.doc: Headers follow one consistent tier scheme.

gate_checks.label: Duplicate headers
gate_checks.doc: No sheet repeats a header without a reason.

gate_checks.label: Frozen headers
gate_checks.doc: Headers stay visible while scrolling.

gate_checks.label: Filters
gate_checks.doc: Tables that are longer than a screen carry a filter.

gate_checks.label: Print setup
gate_checks.doc: Every sheet prints on a readable page layout.

gate_checks.label: Tab colours
gate_checks.doc: Sheet tabs follow the colour scheme of their group.

gate_checks.label: Language
gate_checks.doc: Each workbook is written in one language.

gate_checks.label: Filters without a match
gate_checks.doc: A filter value matches at least one row of its sheet.

gate_checks.label: Cached values
gate_checks.doc: Formulas carry their last result, so that viewers without a calculation engine show numbers.

## Where we are
The estimate is built. Two scenarios: SAP Commerce Cloud and Shopware, each with the Integration Suite per shop option, SAP Customer Data Cloud, Magnolia (CMS agency) and UX/UI design (UX team).

## Confirmed so far
- Your requirement list is carried through unchanged; the effort per system stands beside every row.
- The four gaps are decided: TA-01 back to SAP Customer Data Cloud, TA-02 to the Integration Suite, TA-03 to SAP BTP (your input), IF-03 reduced to the nightly points.

## Open inputs
- CMS agency 3 cells, UX team 4 cells, your SAP BTP cell 1 - about 12 % of the work packages.

## Decisions that would help most
- Confirm or deny A-02 (SAP BTP) and A-03 (nightly points).

events.narrative:
## Where we are
The estimate passed the final gate in round 2 and is ready for the client.

## Confirmed so far
- Scenario SAP Commerce Cloud carries the first release with less development effort than Shopware; the guided finder and the order states drive the difference.
- Every gap is decided and explained on the completeness sheet.

## Open inputs
- CMS agency 3 cells, UX team 4 cells, your SAP BTP cell 1; they sit in both scenarios alike and cannot change their order.

## Decisions that would help most
- Confirm or deny A-02 (SAP BTP) and A-03 (nightly points).

cto.text: Per system: what is standard, what an extension inside the system, what a gap - and does the approach follow from the basis shown on the row?
Can I trace every size to its basis - vendor source, the owner's input or an assumption - without asking?
Where did each gap go (another system of this estimate, a system outside it, a reduction to the standard), and is the decision explained?

head_of_ecommerce.text: What changes in each system for our customers and editors, and do I find our own requirement list with the effort per system beside it?
Which assumptions about our requirements do I have to confirm or deny, and what happens to the estimate if I deny one?
Which scenario carries the first release with less effort, and where do the scenarios differ most per epic?

product_owner.text: Can I plan a backlog per system from the estimation: every work package with a size, every XXL cut into sprint-sized positions?
For a broadly written requirement: which reading does the estimate take, and is it registered as an assumption I can confirm?
What is open and with whom: which cells do partners, the client or the team still have to fill, and which rows depend on a condition?

cfo.text: What is the total per scenario - development, surcharges, fixed phases, person days and cost at the day rate - and does it follow from the workbook's formulas?
What drives the difference between the scenarios: which systems, which epics, which phases?
Which assumptions move the totals, and can I change a parameter (day rate, size mapping, surcharge, range, scenario) and see every total follow?
In the selected scenario, are the costs per system and phase traceable?
What is open and with whom, and can an open input change the order of the scenarios?
